spans.text: Thank—בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֱלֹהֵינוּ שֶׁבְּרָאָנוּ לִכְבוֹדוֹ You for creating us as Your unique nation and giving us a Torah of truth. Open our hearts to Your Torah and inspire us to do the right things! And may we live to see the coming of Mashiach. בְּרוּךְ הַגֶּבֶר אֲשֶׁר—יִבְטַח Blessed is the person who truly trusts in Hashem and is secure in his belief that all Hashem does is for his best (even if it is hard to see). Hashem never abandons those who seek Him.

לְשֵׁם יְחוּד—I am prepared and ready to fulfill the mitzvah of counting the Omer as described in the Torah. (And as Moshe told Bnei Yisrael upon the completion of the Mishkan:) וִיהִי נוֹעַם—May we always feel the pleasantness of the Divine Presence, and may the Divine Presence always rest on the work of our hands.

בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהוָה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; אֱלֹהֵינוּ—You take care of us; מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם—and You rule the entire world; אֲשֶׁר—and וְצִוָּנוּ עַל סְפִירַת הָעֹמֶר—קִדְּשָׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתָיו and through Your mitzvos You elevated us; commanded us concerning the mitzvah of counting the Omer.
May Hashem—הָרַחֲמָן הוּא יַחֲזִיר לָנוּ rebuild the Beis Hamikdash soon and restore the avodah (so that we will actually be able to bring the Korban Omer!).

The focus of this chapter is on the future, when the entire world will join with Bnei Yisrael to sing praises to Hashem and submit to His Will. In addition, after the introductory pasuk, this chapter has forty-nine words, corresponding to the forty-nine days of the Omer!

לַמְנַצֵּחַ בִּנְגִינוֹת—The entire world will understand Your ways, Hashem—and everyone will bow to You and praise You! All the nations will rejoice, because they will understand that You judge everyone fairly. At that time, the earth will produce plenty, and everyone will be blessed and will serve Hashem.

אָנָּא בְּכֹחַ—Please, Hashem, set us, Your chosen nation, free (from our galus)! Accept our tefillos and give us strength (to overcome our challenges); purify us (from all the impurities of the society around us); and guide us (to make the correct decisions). (And even if we do not know how to express ourselves properly) please accept our requests, for You know all our thoughts!
בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ—May the perception of Hashem's Presence and rulership be increased (so all humans will recognize His existence and power); לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד—forever and ever.

רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם—You commanded us to count the Omer from Pesach to Shavuos as an opportunity to reflect, rethink our values, and step by step, day by day, purify ourselves and thus be prepared to accept the Torah again, and our mission to the world, on Shavuos. Hashem, in the merit of this mitzvah of counting the Omer today, may I be cleansed of my impurities, and may I be able to connect to the essence of my neshamah, which is rooted in the Heavens above.
Count the appropriate day; see below.
